summary: Reverified s1_joint_idea_fluency_human_ai_vs_human_only against the paper and extraction rules. Read all 380 lines of the markdown conversion through the final references; the ten-page paper contains no appendix. Extracted the cited PDF pages with PyMuPDF and checked the surrounding methods and results. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 425), section 4, confirms 26 analyzed participants in human+AI, 26 in human-only, and 52 total after exclusions; no different sample is specified for the joint-quantity comparison. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 427), section 5.1, explicitly reports that the human and AI jointly produced significantly more ideas than the human alone. The paper supplies no numerical test or uncertainty for that claim and does not establish its analysis unit, so the null statistics, null unit and n_units, and se_basis=not_reported are appropriate. The question, construct, measure, direction, AI availability, timing, within-person status and comparison type are consistent with a with_ai fluency/category_count outcome produced immediately in separate human+AI and human-only arms. The accepted-versus-logged definition remains uncertain and is already documented; Table 2 includes unaccepted AI suggestions and cannot establish the joint submitted-output statistics. The other four extracted outcomes and the exclusions account for the remaining reported analyses. No additional in-scope outcome or contrast is missing under extraction rules 4-6.
